intro: The writing bank. Every entry is a piece you can only write after building the thing — which is the point, and the reason none of these read like the tutorials already ranking for them. Duplicates from the earlier lists have been merged; where a topic appeared twice the stronger framing was kept.

groups.title: EVM internals and low-level Solidity
groups.note: The layer where findings come from. All of these are demonstrable in a Foundry test, which is what makes them publishable rather than restated.

items.t: data, calldata, memory and storage: what each actually costs
items.d: The four locations as one mental model, priced in gas, with a test showing where a wrong choice doubles a function's cost.

items.t: Visualising the EVM stack
items.d: Step a single transaction and render the stack at each opcode. The diagram you wish someone had shown you.

items.t: uint256 and two's complement: how the EVM represents signed numbers
items.d: Why int256(-1) is a wall of f's, and the casting bugs that follow from not knowing it.

items.t: What bytecode is — creation code, runtime code, and delegatecall instances
items.d: Three things people call 'the bytecode'. Separating them explains why constructors do not exist at runtime.

items.t: Ethereum contract creation code, explained by building one
items.d: Hand-write the init code that returns runtime code, and deploy it without a compiler.

items.t: Offsets in bytecode: reading a jump table by hand
items.d: Where the function dispatcher lives and how a selector becomes a jump.

items.t: Practising assembly revert with real snippets
items.d: Reverting from Yul with correctly encoded error data, which is where most hand-written assembly quietly gets it wrong.

items.t: Writing to any storage slot: when private is not private
items.d: Read and overwrite a private variable with vm.load and vm.store. Private is a compiler convention, not a guarantee.

items.t: Transient storage (tstore/tload) versus regular storage
items.d: What EIP-1153 changed for reentrancy guards and what it costs compared to a storage slot.

items.t: The 63/64 gas rule and why reentrancy guards sometimes fail
items.d: Gas forwarding semantics, and the fallback-based guard that breaks because of them.

items.t: Bitwise operators for gas savings: flags in a single uint256
items.d: Packing booleans into one slot, with the before-and-after gas table.

items.t: Cache values to avoid duplicated SLOADs
items.d: The optimisation Initializable.sol applies, measured, so the advice stops being folklore.

items.t: Why custom errors are cheaper, illustrated rather than asserted
items.d: Compare revert strings, require strings and custom errors at the bytecode level and in gas.

items.t: Gas in ETH, in USD, and per thousand users
items.d: Translating gas units into a number a product manager can act on. The missing article in every optimisation guide.

items.t: Gas optimisation in assembly Solidity
items.d: Where dropping to Yul actually wins, and the cases where the optimiser already did it for you.

items.t: The birthday paradox, for people who collide hashes
items.d: Why 4-byte selectors collide sooner than intuition says, with the arithmetic done out loud.

items.t: Building a function selector checker tool
items.d: A small CLI that detects clashing selectors across an interface set. Ships as a repo, not just an article.

groups.title: Proxies and upgradeability — the series
groups.note: Your deepest existing cluster, and worth publishing as an ordered series rather than scattered posts. Each pattern gets one piece with runnable code, and the series index becomes the thing people link to.

items.t: Storage collisions in upgradeable contracts: how proxies really work
items.d: Deploy a UUPS proxy, add a variable in the wrong slot, and catch the collision in a Foundry test rather than describing it.

items.t: Writing a minimal proxy (EIP-1167) from scratch in assembly
items.d: Implement clone() with mload and mstore, no OpenZeppelin. Deploy a hundred and compare gas against OZ.

items.t: A practical implementation of the beacon proxy
items.d: The pattern for upgrading many instances at once, built and then upgraded live in a test.

items.t: Transparent versus UUPS: rewriting TUPP from first principles
items.d: Both patterns implemented side by side, with the admin-collision problem transparent proxies exist to solve.

items.t: Practical vulnerabilities in UUPS
items.d: Uninitialised implementations, missing _authorizeUpgrade, and the self-destruct path that bricks everything.

items.t: Upgradeable bugs via initialisation
items.d: Initializer versus constructor, re-initialisation, and the reinitializer modifier people misuse.

items.t: Constructors versus initializers
items.d: Why constructor state never reaches the proxy, told through a contract that works standalone and breaks behind one.

items.t: Explaining and writing OpenZeppelin's Initializable.sol
items.d: Read the real implementation line by line, then write your own and diff the decisions.

items.t: ERC-7201 namespaced storage, in your own words
items.d: The layout scheme that makes collisions structurally impossible, and why it took so long to arrive.

items.t: Where the bytecode lives for each proxy type
items.d: Minimal, transparent, UUPS and beacon — which contract holds what, and what an explorer shows you.

items.t: Malicious backdoors in Ethereum proxies
items.d: Work the Nomic Foundation exercise: steal the testnet ETH, then explain the delegatecall mechanism that allowed it.

items.t: When to use delegatecall instead of a library
items.d: Both compile to similar call shapes; the storage context is the whole difference.

items.t: The delegatecall sandbox: a multi-delegatecall router
items.d: Accept a list of targets and calldata, execute all, inspect final storage. Test with two logic contracts.

items.t: Practising the OpenZeppelin upgrade plugins with Foundry
items.d: The safety checks the plugins run, and what each one catches that a human reviewer misses.

items.t: The fallback extension pattern, and changing the extension
items.d: The step most write-ups skip — demonstrating an extension swap rather than only the initial wiring.

items.t: IDiamondLoupe and the DiamondCut event controversy
items.d: Why the loupe is mandated, who objects, and what you lose by omitting it.

items.t: Implementing a DiamondLoupe
items.d: The introspection interface built from scratch, with the facet enumeration that makes diamonds auditable.

items.t: Storage collisions in diamond proxies
items.d: Diamond storage, app storage, and the collision classes unique to multi-facet layouts.

groups.title: Standards and token mechanics
groups.note: Integrations fail at standard boundaries far more often than inside protocol logic. These are the pieces that get cited in audit reports.

items.t: ERC-20 API: an attack vector on approve and transferFrom
items.d: The race between approve and spend, why it was never fixed, and what increaseAllowance actually buys.

items.t: ERC-20 versus SafeERC20
items.d: Non-standard returns, USDT, and the wrapper that exists because the standard was under-specified.

items.t: ERC-20 permit: gasless approvals done right, and wrong
items.d: Build a permit flow, then break it with a wrong v value and missing domain separator replay protection.

items.t: Forging signatures off-chain: EIP-712 and ecrecover pitfalls
items.d: Malleability, signer recovery of the wrong address, and the domain binding that stops cross-chain replay.

items.t: Explaining ERC-1155
items.d: Batch semantics and the callback surface, written for someone who already knows ERC-721.

items.t: Explaining ERC-6909
items.d: The minimal multi-token standard and the ERC-1155 complexity it refuses.

items.t: ERC-777 and the hooks that reintroduced reentrancy
items.d: A standard that made token transfers call untrusted code, and the incidents that followed.

items.t: ERC-4626 and the inflation attack: three real defences
items.d: Virtual shares, dead shares and minimum deposits, each implemented and each attacked.

items.t: Hashing wars: keccak256(abi.encode) versus abi.encodePacked
items.d: The collision that packed encoding permits, shown with two different inputs producing one hash.

items.t: Encoding attacks: abi.decode with malicious calldata
items.d: What happens when decoded length fields lie, and why decoding untrusted bytes is a trust boundary.

items.t: Is there calldata when ether is transferred?
items.d: When calldata exists on a plain transfer, when it does not, and whether it decodes to anything human-readable.

items.t: Explaining calldata and why we use it
items.d: Immutability, cost, and the cases where memory is the only legal choice.

items.t: Why interfaces exist in Solidity
items.d: Type safety across contract boundaries and the ABI they generate — written for people who copy them without knowing why.

items.t: When to use structs and enums
items.d: Packing, readability and the storage cost each choice commits you to.

items.t: Libraries and abstract contracts in Solidity
items.d: Internal versus external libraries, linking, and when inheritance is the wrong tool.

items.t: EIP-2930 optional access lists, in your own words
items.d: Pre-declaring the slots you touch, what it saves, and why almost nobody uses it.

groups.title: DeFi protocol mechanics
groups.note: Uniswap is the reference implementation most DeFi is derived from. Understanding it precisely is the fastest route to reading everything else.

items.t: Retelling the Uniswap V2 swap function
items.d: Walk the real function line by line, including the optimistic transfer that makes flash swaps possible.

items.t: Uniswap V2 flash swap: borrow first, pay later
items.d: Build one, then show the invariant check that makes repayment non-optional.

items.t: Minimal AMM: constant product versus constant sum
items.d: Two curves implemented side by side, with the slippage profile each produces.

items.t: Uniswap V3 and V4 ticks
items.d: Concentrated liquidity as a data structure — tick spacing, crossing, and what a position actually owns.

items.t: The mathematical relationship between Q64.96, ticks and price
items.d: The fixed-point representation that confuses everyone, derived rather than quoted.

items.t: How sqrtPriceLimitX96 defines slippage in Uniswap V4
items.d: The parameter most integrators pass as zero, and what that silently permits.

items.t: A minimal oracle with Uniswap V3 TWAP
items.d: Build it, then show the manipulation window a short observation period leaves open.

items.t: What vaults are, and why EVM architecture keeps reaching for them
items.d: Share accounting, rounding direction, and the ERC-4626 surface that follows.

items.t: What factory patterns are
items.d: Deterministic deployment, registry, and the access control a factory concentrates.

items.t: Adapters in Web3
items.d: The integration layer between protocols, and why adapters are where composability bugs live.

items.t: Building a leverage loop in a single transaction
items.d: Borrow, swap, re-deposit, repeat — with the health factor maths that decides when it stops.

items.t: Pull repayment
items.d: Why pushing funds to users is a reentrancy and griefing surface, and what pulling costs in UX.

items.t: Checks-Effects-Interactions in Solidity
items.d: The ordering rule, the cases where it is insufficient, and why guards are not a substitute.

items.t: How to use the onlyOwner modifier — and when not to
items.d: Single-owner access control, its failure modes, and the step up to roles and timelocks.

items.t: Building a time lock with queue and execute
items.d: Delay, grace period and cancellation, with the governance attack a missing grace period enables.

items.t: A time lock with multi-sig execution
items.d: Combining threshold signing with delay, and the operational trade-off between the two.

items.t: Building a minimal multisig from scratch, no OpenZeppelin
items.d: Signature collection, ordering and replay protection implemented by hand.

items.t: Multi-call batching: building your own multicall
items.d: Aggregating calls, and the msg.sender subtlety that makes naive implementations dangerous.

items.t: Is Circle Arc truly permissionless?
items.d: Read the contracts rather than the announcement, and say what the permissions actually are.

groups.title: Attack patterns and defences

items.t: Reentrancy, beyond the canonical example

items.t: create2 versus create: precomputing addresses before deployment

items.t: Creating a contract from another contract

items.t: Hiding malicious code in external contracts
items.d: Upgradeable dependencies and delegatecall targets as a supply-chain surface.

items.t: Governance as an attack vector

groups.title: Twelve-week build roadmap
groups.note: One protocol a week, built small and audited. Each week produces a repo, an article and an audit checklist — which is three artifacts from one piece of work.

items.t: Week 1 — Yul assembly
items.d: Project: a minimal ERC-20 in pure Yul. Checklist: memory safety, selector dispatch, revert encoding.

items.t: Week 2 — ERC and EIP standards
items.d: Project: implement ERC-20, 721, 1155 and 4626 from the specs, not from OpenZeppelin. Checklist: return values, hooks, rounding.

items.t: Week 3 — DEX (Uniswap V2 mini)
items.d: Project: pair, factory, router. Checklist: K invariant, fee-on-transfer tokens, reserve sync.

items.t: Week 4 — Lending protocol (Aave-lite)
items.d: Project: supply, borrow, liquidate. Checklist: oracle staleness, health factor rounding, bad debt.

items.t: Week 5 — Yield and staking
items.d: Project: a reward distributor with per-second accrual. Checklist: precision loss, reward griefing, exit timing.

items.t: Week 6 — Stablecoin (DAI-lite)
items.d: Project: collateralised debt positions with liquidation. Checklist: peg mechanics, auction design, oracle dependence.

items.t: Week 7 — Derivatives and synthetics
items.d: Project: a perpetual with funding rate. Checklist: mark versus index, funding manipulation, insurance fund.

items.t: Week 8 — AI and NFTs
items.d: Project: generative metadata with on-chain provenance. Checklist: randomness, metadata mutability, royalty enforcement.

items.t: Week 9 — Insurance protocol
items.d: Project: cover purchase and claims assessment. Checklist: claim oracle trust, capital adequacy, correlated risk.

items.t: Week 10 — Asset management and vault strategies
items.d: Project: an ERC-4626 vault with a strategy adapter. Checklist: inflation attack, strategy trust, withdrawal queue.

items.t: Week 11 — Bridges and interoperability
items.d: Project: a mock bridge with a relayer. Checklist: message replay, verification trust, liveness failure.

items.t: Week 12 — DAO and governance
items.d: Project: proposal, vote, timelock, execute. Checklist: flash-loan voting, quorum gaming, execution window.
